title: Make with AI on My Cuff or Bag
sentence: Choose a cuff or bag corner, see an AI pattern preview, then fold or reposition the fabric to guide its next response.
rq: What makes an AI-adapted pattern on a personal item feel connected to its heritage source?
purpose: We follow how a pattern moves from a named source work into someone’s everyday life. A visitor can value a familiar shape, a material relationship, the artist’s story or a personal memory. Their actions and reasons show which connection matters.
steps: Choose a source and item
Look at the named textile work and its background. Point to one detail, then choose a sleeve cuff or bag corner. A plain study item is available.
Frame one local area
Place the item inside the fixed tabletop window. Check the crop preview, then press Capture. Only this selected crop C1 enters the image request and study record.
See the first response
AI uses the source detail and C1 to propose a digital pattern adaptation G1 on the local item. The screen keeps the source, captured crop and generated preview visible together.
Respond with an action
Fold the cuff, flatten a bag edge or reposition the fabric after seeing G1. Capture C2 in the same window when ready. You can also keep G1.
Compare and choose
AI responds to C2 as G2. Compare the two previews and point to a change that matters. Explain briefly what connects it to the source or your own life.
Discuss and keep a record
Use the previews and a fictional future label to discuss changing museum works. Keep a visual record with source credit and your selected version.
ai: A visual partner during the local material action. It proposes a pattern adaptation for the captured cuff or bag area, using a fixed source detail. The visitor’s next fold or position becomes its next input. Added patterns appear in digital previews.
noai: Compare the source with the selected local item, try a fold or position and keep a source-labelled local-item record. Record the visitor’s choice and reason. This route contributes accounts of participation and source connection.
theory: Relational authenticity asks how a connection becomes meaningful through objects, people, making and history. We follow the connections visitors themselves describe.
Looking alike and having a real link
A similar shape is one possible reason. A known maker, source or history gives another kind of link. The personal item and original work each retain their own materials and histories.

We examine whether a visitor can see how their material action affects AI, guide the next image and decide when the result no longer fits the source. Embodied generation already has published precedents.
future: Imagine a museum that shares a textile work as changing digital patterns for visitors’ own cuffs and bags. Its label says “Each version continues the original work”. Looking at your two previews, what would you keep, change or rename in that museum?
speculation: The two actual previews and the clearly fictional label make this future museum concrete. Visitors can discuss how personal use carries a source forward, what should remain recognisable and how the artist and source should be credited. Their own answer guides the discussion.
record: Save source S and its selected detail, item type and capture route, approved crops C1 and C2, actual previews G1 and G2, the action between them, pointed regions, brief reasons and keep or stop decisions. Record model settings, timing, help and failures. Keep future-scenario answers as a separate part of the session.
analysis: Follow S → C1 → G1 → action → C2 → G2 → reason. Read how the visitor relates a change to the source and the personal item. Analyse visual preference, useful control, authorship and source connection as separate judgments. Include choices to keep, stop or use another input route.
value: The candidate contribution is an account of how visitors maintain or change their grounds for a connection to one named heritage object during material interaction with AI. The interaction technique has close precedents. A contribution would need evidence from the action sequence and the visitor’s reasons.
setup: One permitted source detail and fact card, a fixed camera, a small tabletop window, one screen and one image-conditioned generation service. Visitors choose a cuff or bag corner. A plain study cuff or bag panel provides an alternative. Begin with two deliberate captures.
broad: Offer seated access, a plain study item and a helper who follows the visitor’s directions. People can point, speak or select a prepared outline. Explain and record the chosen capture route. AI use remains a choice.
checkpoint: First establish that visitors can see a useful relationship between their local action and the next preview. Then examine whether their reasons refer to the source work, its context, the item or personal experience. Use pilot observations to improve structural guidance and reflection prompts.

title: One Object, Two Interpretations
time: 6–10 minutes per turn, plus an optional postcard
sentence: Start a postcard on a cuff or bag corner, exchange it with a real visitor across languages, then clarify and keep the version that grows from the conversation.
rq: How do visitors retain and negotiate their understanding of a shared heritage object in AI-assisted cross-language exchanges?
purpose: The postcard is the shared object of the conversation from the first draft. One person expresses a connection between a heritage detail and a personal item. A real recipient responds to that draft. The sender clarifies and updates the same card, which becomes the take-away.
steps: Choose the source and local item
Use the same named work, numbered detail and fact card. Choose a cuff or bag corner and approve one local crop C in the shared capture window. A prepared item or outline is available.
Say what you want to express
In your own language, say one short sentence linking the source detail with the item or an association. Check the words before AI uses them.
Build and share draft P1
AI translates the sentence and proposes a pattern preview for C. A fixed layout keeps the source, original words, translation and AI preview together. Approve what the real recipient may see.
Receive a real reply
The recipient sees P1 and the shared source. They point to a detail, explain their understanding or ask a question. The reply can come from an available partner or a consented earlier exchange.
Clarify the same postcard
Accept the reply, clarify the meaning or keep different readings. Update the words on the same card and request one revised image if useful. Keep P1, the reply and the final version P2 linked.
Keep the conversation’s result

Preview P2 with the chosen words, source credit and AI label. Discuss the future display rule, then choose download or optional one-off email. A card awaiting a real reply is labelled Draft awaiting reply.
ai: A language and image assistant around one developing postcard. It translates the visitor’s checked sentence and proposes a pattern adaptation on the approved cuff or bag crop. After the real reply, it can help express a clarification and update that same preview. Each person’s voice stays identified.
noai: Use direct language skills or study-team translation and a plain postcard showing the source, local-item reference and checked words. The real reply and clarification still develop that same card. Choose translation, image generation and delivery separately.
theory: Follow how the object, a person’s experience and the other visitor become connected through exchange.
Separate the sender’s endorsement of wording, the recipient’s understanding, historical accuracy and the recognition of an interpretation.

Being able to change a translation can help people express themselves. It can also make a conversation take more effort. AI writing suggestions may remove cultural details. These findings help us choose what to observe.
future: Imagine a future museum that shows the final AI-assisted postcards as visitors’ interpretations of an object. Which parts of your developing card should the next visitor see: the final version, the earlier draft and reply, or both?
speculation: Use the actual draft, real reply and final card beside a fictional future-display label. Participants decide how a museum should show a meaning that developed through conversation, and whose words or images should remain visible. The real source and each contributor remain identified.
record: Follow one card ID through source S, local crop C and its sharing choice, initial words M1, identified translation, actual draft P1, real reply R, clarification M2 and final P2. Retain accepted and declined image changes. Delivery choice and job status use a separate restricted record.
analysis: Follow how a particular source detail and meaning travel through the first draft, the recipient’s response and the sender’s clarification. Examine words and images together. Distinguish source accuracy, translation fit, recipient understanding, author approval and personal connection.
value: The candidate contribution is an account of how a source-related personal meaning develops through a multilingual conversation around one AI-assisted visual postcard. Its draft and revision show how people recognise, question and clarify each other’s interpretations. The final card keeps the outcome of that same process.
setup: Use the same fixed capture station as A. Add a short-message interface, a real reply channel or consented reply pool and one postcard template. Start with one draft image and one optional revision. A private delivery service can send the final card in the study deployment.
broad: Allow speech, short text, pointing, a prepared item and study-team language support. Visitors can arrive alone and receive a reply later. Keep the same card ID across turns. Plain cards, downloads and finishing without email are available choices.
checkpoint: Check that a recipient replies to the actual source-linked draft. Follow whether the sender’s clarification changes the words, image or their stated connection to the work. Keep pending replies visible as pending. Test the full draft–reply–clarification–receipt journey.
